grade.first_issue: In Case B, the identity \(f(z+c)=\frac{z f(z)}{z-c}\) is valid only for \(z\ne0,c\), but it is treated as valid for every real \(z\).
grade.summary: The argument correctly derives \(f(x)=-x\) when \(f(0)=0\) and \(f\not\equiv0\), and \(f(x)=c-x\) when \(f(0)=c\ne0\). The only gap is failure to handle \(z=0,c\) explicitly in the final Case B calculation; these exceptional points follow immediately from the already established \(f(0)=c\) and \(f(c)=0\). Verification of all claimed solutions is correct.
strengths: Correctly establishes bijectivity in both nonzero cases and uses it effectively.
Derives the complete solution family and verifies it directly.

errors.description: The final rational identity in Case B excludes \(z=0,c\); those two values are not explicitly restored before claiming the formula for all real \(z\).
